lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-9054 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/rchen
Date of birth: 5 Feb 1998 | Nationality: Singaporean
EDUCATION
Harbor State University | B.B.A. in Finance | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Crescent Bank | Credit Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Dec 2022
- Hedged the bank's interest-rate risk on its fixed-rate bond holdings by buying more fixed-rate bonds of the same duration.
- Reviewed 3 years of declined applications; my findings changed two ratio thresholds and raised approvals from 41% to 48% with no rise in early defaults.
- Writes the covenant-monitoring checklist for the portfolio, cutting missed covenant tests from 7 to 1 a year.
- Built a spreading template for borrower financials that cut each credit memo from 6 hours to 3.
Stonebridge Manufacturing | Financial Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jan 2023 - Jun 2025
- Built the rolling 18-month cash-flow forecast for a USD 600M manufacturer, keeping monthly forecast error under 4% and letting treasury pay down USD 40M of revolver debt early.
- Cut the monthly close from 8 working days to 5 by automating 30 reconciliations and intercompany eliminations.
- Modeled the capital plan for 12 plant projects in a shared NPV template, so every request used the same discount rate and payback rules.
- Mapping 600 general-ledger accounts to a new chart of accounts, rebuilding the allocation rules and testing them against two prior closes, cut manual journal entries from 350 to 90 a month.
- Valued the acquisition target by discounting its free cash flow to equity at the company's weighted average cost of capital.
- Trained 5 plant controllers on the new budgeting template and wrote its user guide.
PROJECTS
Regional Utility Valuation | Independent Project | Excel | Nov 2024 - Present
- Valued a listed regional utility with a 10-year DCF and a comparable-company check, landing within 6% of the market price.
- Showed the share value fell from USD 50 to USD 40, a 25% drop, when the discount rate rose by 1 point.
- Raised the model's forecast accuracy by 12% across 10 years, from 70% to 82%, by adding rate-case timing.
Student Investment Fund | Analyst, Team of 6 | Excel | Sep 2018 - May 2019
- Supported the FP&A team with financial reporting and analysis.
- Rebuilt the fund's performance report to show returns against its benchmark, which the committee used at every meeting.
- Wrote onboarding notes on the fund's models for new analysts.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel
Methods: financial modeling, DCF valuation, forecasting, credit analysis

items.says: The résumé includes a date of birth and nationality.
items.because: These details are unrelated to job performance and can introduce protected personal information.

items.says: Education leads the résumé despite five years of professional experience.
items.because: Recent finance roles provide stronger evidence, so the current order delays the material hiring managers are most likely to weigh.

items.says: The Experience section is not in reverse chronological order.
items.because: Crescent Bank ended before Stonebridge, so listing it first delays the most recent experience.

items.says: Buying more fixed-rate bonds of the same duration does not hedge the existing holdings’ interest-rate risk.
items.because: It increases same-direction duration exposure rather than providing an offsetting position.

items.says: The hedging claim does not quantify how much the exposure changed.
items.because: Without a before-and-after risk measure, the reader cannot judge its effectiveness or materiality.

items.says: The strongest underwriting result is not first in the Crescent Bank entry.
items.because: Burying the approval-rate result makes the entry scan as unrelated tasks rather than coherent credit analysis.

items.says: “No rise in early defaults” omits the default rate and measurement period.
items.because: The reader cannot tell how much credit performance was observed or whether the approvals had time to season.

items.says: “Reviewed 3 years of declined applications” does not identify what was analyzed.
“My findings” unnecessarily shifts the résumé into first person.
“Writes” presents completed work as current despite the role ending in December 2022.
items.because: The present tense conflicts with the employment dates and past tense elsewhere in the entry.

items.says: “Covenant-monitoring checklist” does not identify the control that prevented missed tests.
“Spreading template for borrower financials” does not show what it automated or standardized.
“Cut each credit memo from 6 hours to 3” treats the memo itself as a duration.
“Letting treasury pay down” is informal and states the causal relationship imprecisely.
The bullet does not explain how the reconciliations and eliminations were automated.
Using the same discount rate and payback rules shows consistency without stating what it improved.
“So every request used” describes the standardization conversationally and loosely.
The reduction in manual journal entries is buried behind a long description of the method.
items.because: A scanning reader must pass through the method before reaching the strongest evidence of value.

items.says: “Them” does not make clear whether the accounts or allocation rules were tested.
The valuation discounts free cash flow to equity at weighted average cost of capital.
items.because: FCFE requires a cost of equity; WACC applies to unlevered free cash flow to the firm.

items.says: “The company’s” does not identify whether the discount rate belongs to Stonebridge or the target.
items.because: The relevant entity affects the appropriate valuation inputs and makes the method harder to assess.

items.says: The valuation does not state what decision or deal action it informed.
items.because: Without a consequence, it reads as a deliverable rather than demonstrated business influence.

items.says: The training and user-guide bullet does not state whether the work improved adoption, accuracy, rework, or cycle time.
“Within 6% of the market price” omits the direction of the difference and the benchmark date.
items.because: The reader needs to know whether the model indicated upside or downside and which market price was compared.

items.says: “Valued” is inconsistent with a project dated through “Present.”
The stated 25% drop from USD 50 to USD 40 is mathematically incorrect.
items.because: The USD 10 decline is 20% of the original USD 50 value.

items.says: “Discount rate” does not identify whether the model used WACC, cost of equity, or another rate.
items.because: The rate depends on the modeled cash flow and is central to checking the DCF mechanics.

items.says: “Rose by 1 point” leaves the unit of the rate change ambiguous.
items.because: One percentage point differs materially from one basis point.

items.says: “Showed” is inconsistent with a project dated through “Present.”
“Accuracy by 12%” misstates the increase from 70% to 82%.
items.because: The change is 12 percentage points, or approximately 17.1% relative to the original value.

items.says: “Forecast accuracy” and “across 10 years” do not define the metric, comparison data, or evaluation design.
items.because: The reader cannot interpret or reproduce the improvement or tell whether the period was a historical back-test.

items.says: “Adding rate-case timing” does not explain how that input changed the forecast.
“Raised” is inconsistent with a project dated through “Present.”
“Financial reporting and analysis” does not identify the deliverable or analytical work performed.
items.because: The reader cannot tell what task was done or what skill the line demonstrates.

items.says: “Supported the FP&A team” does not state what the work enabled or improved.
items.because: Without an outcome, the line remains a duty rather than evidence of contribution.

items.says: The strongest line in the Student Investment Fund entry is not first.
items.because: The benchmark report shows a defined output and repeated committee use, unlike the generic opening line.

items.says: “Its benchmark” does not identify the index or benchmark used.
items.because: The benchmark determines whether the comparison was appropriate for the fund’s mandate.

items.says: “Rebuilt the fund’s performance report” does not show what changed technically or analytically.
“Which” could refer to the benchmark rather than the performance report.
“The fund’s models” does not identify which models or components were documented.
items.because: The generic reference gives little evidence of the financial knowledge transferred.

items.says: The line identifies the notes’ audience but not their effect.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether they shortened onboarding, reduced errors, or improved independent model use.

items.says: The Student Investment Fund entry is padded by generic support and onboarding duties.
items.because: Those lines lack the benchmark report’s specificity and take space from more current finance and valuation evidence.
